First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{3}+C) \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{1}{3}(x+3C))\end{aligned}
$$

The factor $x+3C$ indicates that the graph of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{1}{3}(x+3C))$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{3}).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186184149/plots/e5690a634385eeb22814479d-solution.png)

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{3})$ by $\frac{9\pi }{7}$ units to the right. Therefore:

$$
3C=-\frac{9\pi }{7}\,⟹\,C=-\frac{3\pi }{7}
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $-\frac{3\pi }{7}$ is in this interval, the value of $C$ is $-\frac{3\pi }{7}.$
